reference_sql:
SELECT s.currency, COUNT(*) AS invoices, SUM(i.amount_local / 12) AS renewal_mrr
FROM invoices i
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.subscription_id = i.subscription_id
WHERE s.billing_period = 'annual'
  AND i.invoice_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  AND month(i.invoice_date) = month(s.start_date)
  AND day(i.invoice_date) = day(s.start_date)
GROUP BY s.currency

WITH annual AS (
  -- one row per annual subscription
  SELECT subscription_id, currency, start_date
  FROM subscriptions
  WHERE billing_period = 'annual'
)
SELECT a.currency, COUNT(*) AS invoices, SUM(i.amount_local / 12) AS renewal_mrr
FROM invoices i
JOIN annual a ON a.subscription_id = i.subscription_id
WHERE i.invoice_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  AND date_diff('month', a.start_date, i.invoice_date) % 12 = 0
  AND day(i.invoice_date) = day(a.start_date)
GROUP BY a.currency

SELECT a.currency, COUNT(*) AS invoices, SUM(i.amount_local / 12) AS renewal_mrr

WHERE i.invoice_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  AND date_diff('month', a.start_date, i.invoice_date) % 12 = 0
  AND day(i.invoice_date) = day(a.start_date)
GROUP BY a.currency
other_way.tradeoff: A month count that is a whole number of years picks the same invoices, but date_diff counts month boundaries, so the day test stays.
